main_text.p: toris Iustiniani iram sopiendam {f}Lega-tione fungeretur:in qua obeunda,eum cum Imperatore familiariter collocutũ legimus, neq; alia puto Iustinianum lingua vsum præter Græcam,quum & ipsi vernacula, siue materna fuerit, & (teste Cuspiniano & Suida)esset ipse ἀναλφάβητος, omnium scilicet & artium & Linguarũ prorsus expers.Neq; tum temporis minus vsitata crediderim Romanis præsertim doctioribus linguam Græca (propter frequentes & assiduũ cum orientalibus comercium) quam occidentalibus hodie lingua latina,quam tamen è Germanis, Gallis, Anglis purissimè semper & loquuti sunt & scripserũt aliqui, vt vt sit, Baronio de stylo Græco Criticũ agenti, non nimis credendũ arbitror, cum suos Tractatus Græcos,in Bibliotheca Vaticana repertos,alijs transferedos dedisse, passim fateatur.Postremò,ꝑ[?] ad Authorem huius opusculi obscurandũ afferat ex Actis Synodi Constantinopolitanæ sub Menna[?], constare duos claruisse Agapetos vtrofq; Monasteriorũ Archimandritas,potiùs hoc factum judico (vt rectè idẽ prius obseruauit Index Expur-

page.notes: Left margin note "f Zonaras." is printed in small type beside the first line; it is placed as a foot note keyed to the mark "f" in the text, not in a margin tag, because the mark in the text is the same letter. The symbol after "Postremò," and the word after "sub" are doubtful. The Greek word ἀναλφάβητος is copied as best read. The right printed page is cut off at the scan edge: only line ends such as "gat", "cju", "fcr", "nih", "gra", "mi", "qui", "Th", "n°", "Ro", "om", "qu", "net", "rer", "Ee", "ξo", "cis", "tar", "et", "de", "toa", "ne", "et", "ler", "in", "tic", "et" and a header letter "L" are visible. These fragments are not transcribed as text, since they are too cut off to read reliably and do not form words.
